title: Billing Bulletin on Payer Recoupment of a Shipped PAP Supply Replenishment Program Line
content:
A recoupment by a payer of a paid item line in the PAP Supply Replenishment Program is recorded against that line as the original line, one reversal per line named by the payer; a paid line is reversed at most once.

## Effects of a reversal

- The reversed line no longer counts toward the item's current covered-through date.
- Every patient charge stemming from the reversed line is removed under the rules of Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility.

## Once per line

Whether a line has already been reversed is read from the enrollment's shipment records: a reversal already naming the same original line.

| Reversals already naming the paid line | A new reversal of that line |
|---|---|
| none | recorded against the line named by the payer |
| one | not recorded — the line is reversed at most once |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A payer takes back a paid headgear line. The reversal is recorded against that headgear line. From then on, that line no longer counts when the headgear's current covered-through date is read, and any patient charge that arose from it is removed under the coverage rules. If the payer later names the same line again, no second reversal is recorded.
